BiblicalUsage: The true one, the real thing as opposed to the copy. John calls Christ the true Light which lighteth every man that cometh into the world, and Jesus calls Himself the true vine, and His Father the husbandman. Eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom He has sent. And the risen Christ writes to Philadelphia as He that is holy, He that is true, who opens and no man shuts.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word draws the line between the real and the imitation, and the line runs through Jesus. There are many lights and many vines and many gods, and John says there is one true Light, one true vine, one true God. I hold that knowing Him is not one truth among others — it is the truth that makes everything else true, and eternal life is knowing Him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
